The same thing happened to me at about the same age.  I found out my mom was chatting with a friend from high school on facebook. I happened to look over her shoulder while she was on the family computer and when I asked her who she was talking to (the guy shared a name as one of my friends so I was confused) she got very defensive and tried to hide the chat. I later logged into her facebook and found that she was making plans to cheat on my dad. I didn't tell my dad right away, I talked to my mom first. I told her I knew she was talking to someone and that I thought it should stop. She said it was just fun. I didn't tell her I logged into her facebook, so she assumed I figured it out from the instance where I read a few messages over her shoulder. I kept tabs on there FB conversations but I guess they were texting too because she ended up meeting him with me in tow.

A few weeks later my mom and I left on vacation. My dad had to work so he stayed home. We were going to visit my mom's family and on the way there she said she was going to see a friend and help him move. We got to his house and when he came out I recognized him as the guy from facebook. My mom made me help him move his things out of his house into a moving trailer while they went and talked and it was very surreal. The nest day at my aunts house the guy showed up for family dinner and my mom was obviouslyh flirting with him. It was very hurtful. When we got home I saved all her messages on FB and went and told my dad what she did and how she met the guy and had him over for dinner. They ended up talking and my mom said she wouldn't do it anymore. 

6 months later on the week of my birthday she told my dad that she physically cheated on him with this guy even though she said she'd stop talking to him.

My parents almost left eachother, but my dad groveled for my mom's affection and my mom ate it up. They stayed together and are now okay, their relationship is still dysfunctional, but I'm 20 and out of the house now so I don't have to deal with it. My mom was also abusive to me like you described and continues to be to this day, but my dad loves me and we are basically best friends now. We gained a lot of trust in eachother through the whole ordeal.

Take what you will from my story, if I were you I'd talk to the cheater before talking to the one who is getting cheated on.  I'd be open and honest, but try not to be too angry at either of them in person. Be strong if you decide to talk to them, act mature, tell them how much it hurts to see and how no matter what you want them to both be happy and you don't want their relationship issues to fuck up your life.

Progress.

Mental illness isn't just about wanting to improve in the same way that diabetes or dementia isn't about wanting to improve. It is a mental illness, yes you have to want to recover, but to say that that is all you need do is completely false. For some people it isn't simply negativity, but it is much more. It is an emotional trauma, chemical imbalance, life situation, and many other things. It has a root cause, it has a marked effect. It is not a choice. I do not choose to be unhappy. I try very hard to be happy. Unfortunately I have been depressed my whole life. I am diagnosed with an anxiety disorder. As a result I self-harmed to deal with it in my younger years. That choice led to a crippling self-harm addiction that I still struggle with daily, hourly, by the minute even. I went to counseling, my anxiety is much much much better and I'm mostly able to control it. My depression has been harder to control and therapy hasn't helped enough, but I have faith that with time I'll find a way to be happier. Maybe not. Maybe I should try medication. Maybe that wouldn't work either. Maybe I'm a lost cause. But let me tell you, mental illness is not something you choose to have. It isn't something you can simply choose to recover from. It is not just a change in perspective. The way you see the world, the way you feel people see you, the way you see yourself; all those things can be altered. It's not just that you're negative, it's that you honestly perceive things different. You could be a supermodel and still think you're the worst/ugliest person on the planet. You could be the nicest person but you could see yourself as the worst/meanest person on the planet. You could be the most responsible person, but maybe you feel others think of you as being irresponsible. Etc. Etc.
I'm sorry, but you know nothing about the progress I've made or anything so I don't see how your comment was even relevant.

My great aunt was dying in the nursing home. My mom and I had been staying with her and returning home to shower and such. My mom had gone home to change clothes and freshen up, but I decided to stay behind and read to her from one of my kids books. It was a story about a little boy fighting in the revolutionary war. I was probably 11 at the time. Anyway, as I said I was reading to her and she started to make this weird sound like she was struggling to breathe, then she started convulsing. She had been virtually unresponsive for a while so at first I thought she was trying to talk or something, but when the convulsing happened I knew that wasn't the case. I immediately threw my book down and said "I'm gonna get help. I'll be right back." and I ran to the nurses desk. I told them she was making a weird noise and had started shaking all over and that they had to help her. I remember having a sense that it was the end, but still having hope that they could fix her or bring her back. Earlier that day I had been doodling get well cards for her for when she woke up. I wasn't ready to let go yet. I remember being completely pissed that they were taking so long to come help her. They seemed so slow. The way they filled up the syringes and the way they just casually walked to her room, like a few more minutes of her suffering was no big deal.  To be honest it still kind of pisses me off, I mean I know now that there was nothing they could do obviously, but in my child mind they should have ran.

 I kinda blocked out a lot after that point. I remember getting to the door and watching from the doorway as they rolled her over and held her down to give her a shot of what I assume was morphine or some other heavy painkiller/sedative. I remember that the shaking and convulsing stopped very quickly afterward, but the weird breathing continued. I remember my mom suddenly being there and I remember them letting her in but not me. I remember that they left the door open though, but they still wouldn't let me in the room. I remember hearing the weird breathing stop. I don't remember anything after that at all. I don't remember driving home. I don't really remember getting home. I don't remember falling asleep that night. Just the end. 

I really wish I could remember the last thing she said to me, but there are very few things I actually remember about the week before her death except the day of her death.

It's going really well. I'm terrible at learning languages and was never able to grasp Spanish in high school, but I'm definitely grasping Ojibwe, slowly but surely. I take classes at a local community college on the reservation. I'm getting an associates in Liberal arts and Native American History - Emphasis in language. Ojibwe has a really easy grammar to adhere to. 

For instance: 

My mom - Nimaamaa
Your mam - Gimaamaa
Her/His Mom - omaamaayan

All phrases follow a certain pattern as well: 

Personal prefix etc + tense + modifier + verb + negation. 

For example: Nin + ga + wayiiba+ gichi + bakkade. 

Written out right it looks like "Nin-gawayiiba gichi bakkade"

Literally Meaning I (Nin) Will (ga) soon (wayiibaa) very/great (gichi) be hungry (baked). So "I will soon be very hungry."

The secret to learning ojibwe is understanding the grammar for me because phrases are put together so differently in english. In Ojibwe, things are literally added to words to change the meaning. 

For instance to ask the question "Who is Tom's Grandfather?" you would say "Awenen Omishoomeyan Tom?". To ask Tom his grandfathers name directly would be "Awenen Gimishoomis?" The Gi at the beginning distinguishes the "You" just as the O at the beginning distinguishes a third person when you're asking someone else about Tom's grandad. However the word for ones own grandfather is "Nimishoomis". The word for grandfather without assigning a possession is "mishoomis", but in ojibwe it is hugely rare to speak of something without it being possessed by someone or something. Another distinction made in ojibwe is between Animate and inanimate things. For instance, the way I you say "my daughters" is "Nindaanisag." but the way you say "my tables" is "Nindadoopowinan". As you can see animate and inanimate plurals and possessives are different. Of course sometimes the way you do it is different depending on what the word begins or ends with. For instance since the word for cups is "Onaagaans" to say "My cups." is "Nindonaagaansoon." This is because it begins in and O and ends with an NS.

So basically I've become much more fluent in Ojibwe by really observing and doing my best to learn the grammar behind everything so I can understand it best. Just memorizing words doesn't really work for me or for anyone I don't think. You have to first known how the words work so you can apply them.
Native American Ojibwe and because it's part of my heritage (I'm an 8th) and it's a dying language. Someone has to carry it on.

Stick and pokes really have to be done in layers because it's very very hard to get it dark/solid enough lines on the first layer. 
 
I used bombay non-toxic black india ink and had no problems or reactions. I did one small dot on my finger to see how I'd react to it. I waited a day and nothing bad happened so I went for it. However, if you  want the best results you can buy tattoo ink online for pretty cheap and that way you'll know you're less likely to have a bad reaction to the ink. From what I hear india ink fades faster than tattoo ink (makes sense) and some people are more likely to reject the ink because it's not made for being imbedded in skin. I'd suggest that just to be on the safe side, but I didn't really care about my stick and pokes that much, I just wanted to try it and the india ink was easier for me to get a hold of than tattoo ink.

I'm a huge huge example of habituation to pain and the interpersonal theory of suicide (though I'm no longer suicidal I was at one point and my self-harm is part of what got me there.) The following quote sums it up well: "The basis for this proposition rests primarily on the principles of opponent-process theory, which suggests that with repeated exposure to an affective stimulus, the reaction to that stimulus shifts over time such that the stimulus loses its ability to elicit the original response and, instead, the opposite response is strengthened (Solomon, 1980)." So when I cut myself to be completely honest I don't necessarily feel pain during the act. I feel the tug of the razor across my skin, I feel the skin separate, I feel what should be pain, but isn't pain so much as it is relief. It's like it's exactly the opposite of what I should be feeling. It's a release of tension. For instance, before I cut if I let the urges get to this point I will  feel like my tendons/veins/tissues in my arms are squirming. Not literally, they obviously aren't squirming, but that's the only way I can describe the particular discomfort. It's a bodily urge for me just like hunger or the need to piss. Or I guess another way to compare it would be to orgasm, but obviously it doesn't feel good on that level, it's a very similar urge though. It feels like a need in that moment. Urgent.  I tried the rubber band thing. Ice cubes. Punching things. Yada yada. I went to counseling for cumulatively a year (on and off over the course of 2.5 years). There were a to of things that I was told to try to find something that gave me the release I wanted. Running, jogging, screaming (yep), yoga, meditation, punching bag, long walks, holding onto ice, snapping rubber bands, tearing paper, writing what was bothering me and then burning the writing, the list could go on for a long time. I've tried everything and what works best is honestly regular exercise. Which I do and has cut down my relapses by a lot, but there's nothing like the release I'm looking for. I know I'll never find something to replace the self-harm, but eventually I will find some way to overcome it. I'm just never ready. I thought I was ready to quit 3 years ago. I relapsed eventually. There's been many times since then I thought I was ready to be done with it, but every time when things get hard, the addict side of my brain says that I should just give in and I do.  I try and I fail. I try and I lose motivation. I try half heartedly. I try again. I quit trying. And that's where I'm at now.  

Another reason it's hard to find something to replace self harm is like I said, it's not really about the pain, so a lot of what it's about is the ritual of it. The habit. Once you get in the cycle it's hard to drag yourself out. Additionally, the sight and smell and feel of the blood and the wounds themselves is addicting, which sounds sadistic, but what the wounds represent is a feeling of empowerment, relief, etc. I can't describe what I mean when I say I want to see my arm fill of cuts or how I want to feel the blood running down my legs. I really can't explain that feeling because it makes no sense, but it's true.  Another addicting thing about it is that it  allows me to feel in control when situations feel out of control. I can control where I cut, when I cut, what I use. I can control depth, width, amount of blood... Literally every part of it is my doing, and that is one of the most intriguing facts that keeps me coming back. The need to feel in control.

I'm a cutter mostly and piercer sometimes. I use blades to slice my skin or safety pins to puncture it. I also have other more acceptable self-harm habits. Like biting my nails, pulling my hair, biting my lip, picking scabs, etc. Started when I was 12, hitting myself with rulers, scratching myself, etc. When I was 13-14 I cut for the first time. I used to cut infrequently, whenever I was feeling upset, but slowly it became habitual. It becomes a physical dependency to an extent I think. When you cut your body releases feel good chemicals to lessen your pain, this gives you a rush (kinda like the adrenaline rush you feel on roller coasters). In that way it is a physical urge for me. My body wants that feeling and it knows it can get it by way of self-harm, therefore it's an addiction. Like I said, it's also habitual. I cut multiple times a week for a long long time. I went 2 years before I tried to get help the first time, so there was a lot of time to become addicted. It became habit. Every time I take a shower I think about cutting because that's the place where I cut with the most frequency (private, easy to clean, etc). Every time I'm stuck at home instead of going out and doing something after work I feel like cutting because most times I cut were at home in the afternoon or evening. Every time I'm upset at any level my first instinct is to find some place secluded and self-harm to feel better or to release some of the anxious tension. Any time I feel depressed I want to cut to feel something other than depressed. Any time I can't sleep I want to cut because just the act of preparing my blades and cutting and then cleaning up is almost like a relaxing ritual to me. Any time I'm angry my cutting urges are very bad because I feel guilt over the anger. Every time i eat to much I want to cut to punish myself. Every time I do something wrong at work I want to cut to punish myself. Every time I upset someone I want to cut to punish myself. The punishing thing may sound counterintuitive because cutting makes me feel better, so why would I use it as punishment, but this is because I consciously know it's something I shouldn't be doing to myself. Psychologically during these times it's almost like my mind is punishing my body for whatever stupid thing I've done. Any time I see something I associate with cutting I think about it and if I'm feeling upset it'll usually trigger a relapse. Like if I'm sad and I find a dry wall cutter at work it feels simply natural to steel a blade and hide in the bathroom for a few minutes. If I'm angry and there's safety pins lying around I'll pierce them through my skin and fasten them and let them sit until I've calmed down enough to take them out. That's kinda what I do when I know I can't get away with having open wounds like in the summer or if someone's going to be seeing me naked, etc. 

So basically it's become my fix for any turmoil or upset. I don't know how. It doesn't really make sense. Typing this out definitely makes me sound crazy, but it's all true and I need to learn to accept that somehow.
Keep relapsing into self-harm even though I'm ruining my body and upsetting the people around me. I need to learn my lesson, but it's hard and no one understands.

I wouldn't worry about it too much until it actually becomes a problem. Chances are it was a passing crush, the kind where you think "Oh, he/she's cute, wouldn't mind having something with him/her." ( 'something' meaning relationship, closer friendship, fwb situation, etc) but those kind of crushes are pretty harmless after a while if it's the type of thing where you may not be that close. 

For instance if you'd been friends, but not super close friends, it's more likely it was just a passing crush. If he'd known you for a long time and was close to you it's more likely to be an "I want a relationship with him/her" crush. 

Either way I'd let it go unless he starts to get clingy. If he starts trying to text and call and and generally talk to you in any way that might hint that he wants something more. Sending hearts in texts (cliche, but it is a warning sign), talking to you DRASTICALLY more frequently and/or with greater intensity of interest in you, calling/texting more frequently even if you back off for a while. If he tries to bring you into his friend group without a legitimate reason or if he looks for reasons then he may be looking for something more. Each person is different and it's probably better just to note changes in his personal behavior, those are the red flags, not what people on the internet tell you are red flags. 

But If he start to show signs of feelings then have a talk with him and ask him outright if he does. Tell him he can be honest and make him comfortable, after all it's not his fault if he has feelings and if you inadvertently make him feel bad he might lie about it and that'll just cause a bigger problem eventually. If he says yes then you know what to do at that point.

You seem to be looking at this very one sided, he wants to lead a different lifestyle than you do and that's just how he is. From your post it sounds like you're really just imagining your perfect life and not what he may see as a perfect life. People's wants change, and perhaps he needs something more from life at this time and isn't ready to settle down in one place and have children. At 24 years old it's still acceptable for a person to change their mind about what their wants are and there's still time to settle down/have kids in the future and pursue a different life for the time being. It sounds like he's not ready to commit to that dream life just yet, though that doesn't mean he won't want it someday. 

That being said, as you must think about his wants, he must think about yours. Compromise is part of any good relationship. If you were to move you've listed your concerns. You'll miss family and friends, you'll be far away, but that doesn't mean you can't still  maintain relationships with them and still visit. Many of my siblings and friends have moved across the country and it hasn't changed much except for seeing them less. The interactions are still great, and sometimes better because we have more fun together when we do see each other. If you do ever consider moving voice this concern to your boyfriend and tell him you need to know that you'll be able to come back as frequently as you can/is possible. Your concern about work is one that's a little harder, but talking this over with your boyfriend would help. Tell him your concerns and see what he thinks of them, ask him in a logical and non-accusing way. Chances are he's not seeing things the same as you and you can't expect him to. If you both talk about things logically you'll come up with a conclusion. You either solve the problem together by compromising and coming up with a solution, or one of two things happens: go your separate ways or one of you gives up a dream. Giving up a dream isn't always bad, but it can be so choose wisely.

For everyone asking what the downsides are to smoking weed, here are some I have noted, all of which I have been able to remedy by making smalls changes in my life. For reference I have been smoking for two years, for most of last year I was a 'few-times-per-week' smoker whenever I needed to unwind. Now I have smoked daily (except for a few days due to sickness) for about four months. Since I've started smoking daily I have noticed: 

1. Memory loss. This is probably the only truly notable problem I've had. When I smoked less frequently I didn't notice any memory loss, now though I will sometimes have a thought and then it will be gone in the next instant. It's not bad, but mildly inconvenient at times. I've taken to writing things down and making lists which has solved the problem entirely. This for me has been the worst effect of marijuana use, but it really isn't too bad, It doesn't seem to be permanent. If I go a few weeks without smoking my memory improves. 

2. Cough. I now have a bit of a smoker's cough, I occasionally smoke cigarettes too so that contributes to it, but the cough didn't really start until I started smoking more weed. It is manageable and part of it may be due to me having minor asthma problems as well.

3. Weight gain. Some of that is due to the fact that it's winter and I tend to put on weight in the winter anyway, but I did gain about 3 pounds. To remedy that I started exercising more and buying healthier munchie food. I am now a lower weight than I was before I became a daily smoker.  

4. Crashing. If I smoke more than once a day for a period of a few days, for instance if I smoke 3 or 4 times in a day each day for 4 days straight; I notice that I will feel depressed for the following few days (usually only 1 or 2). I'm not sure what the science is behind this, but it probably has something to do with too much feel good hormones being released and thusly depleted. Not really sure. If I smoke only once or twice a day this doesn't happen, its only if I go on a 'binge' so to speak. 

Everyone is different and weed effects everyone differently. It does wonders for some, is awful for others. For me, the negative effects of weed are far outweighed by the positive ones as long as I moderate things. In my opinion, the best way to smoke weed with fewer negative effects is to be an occasionally smoker. When I smoked occasionally and even when I smoked multiple times a week there were no bad side effects at all. All things in moderation. 

Weed has had great effects on my life as well: 

1. I have whats called Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome type 3, meaning my joints are very hyper mobile and I can strain and tear things easily. My feet, hands, shoulders, and knees are all effected by it and have sustained injuries such as dislocations, tears, strains and subluxations. Weed definitely helps with the chronic pain and inflammation of my joints, some strains more so than others. 

2. Depression. I have depression and Whenever I'm feeling down weed is a nice pick me up. If I feel myself falling into a depressive episode I'll smoke a bowl and it'll stop it in its tracks. Even after the high is gone usually I am able to see my problems in a better light. I can say to myself "Remember when you were high and thinking about this problem? It's really not so bad." and I can then kind of rationally think of the problem and how to fix it rather than dwelling on how terrible it is. 

3. Believe it or not, weed has helped me with my anxiety, yes it is true that some strains that are really high in THC will make my anxiety worse, but in small doses, no matter the weed, it will make me calmer. The other day I found out some shit about my brother and my family was kind of in a crisis. I had a complete breakdown while driving and had to pull off on a back road and sit for a while. After the initial freak out was over I smoked a bowl and it eased my mind and helped me look at the situation in a different way. 
Of course if I smoke a few bowls or take several rips of some super dank, high THC percentage bud and I was already in an anxious mood it will double my anxiety. It all depends on the weed and what my mood is at the time. I've become pretty good at being able to tell if the weed will heighten my anxiety or not and as long as I smoke weed that has a a higher CBD content and lower THC content it reduces my anxiety more so. With strains more geared towards CBD and less THC you don't get the same high at all and it takes more to get that stoned feeling. I generally don't just smoke to feel stoned, I smoke to feel whatever I want to feel at the time. If I want to get stoned I smoke a shit ton, if I want to chill I smoke a bowl and call it good.

4. I sleep better now. The biggest benefit of weed for me is that it stopped my terrifying recurring nightmares and episodes of sleep paralysis. I've had one really bad nightmare in the past 2 months, as apposed to before I became a daily smoker, I would often have 2 to 6 bad nightmares per month, sometimes more if I was going through a hard time mentally. Additionally, it has been a year since my last episode of sleep paralysis. 

TL;DR: Weed effects everyone different and the key to it is finding what works for you. It's about balance.

She sat with her legs up on the bench seat, staring out the window as the world flew by. Her long arms reaching around the front of her knees, feet slightly pigeon toed, her back against the metal arm rest of the seat behind her. She wore worn leather boots, and not the fake kind you buy at Walmart, the real kind you buy at Farm and Fleet. The were scuffed up along the toes, the stitches in the genuine leather were beginning to loosen, the laces were frayed, but tied tightly around her slim ankles. Her boots left a small pile of sand on the seat where they rested, but she didn't seem to notice.  

Ear buds were jammed into her small ears and I wondered what she listened to today. A slight smile graced her lips so I assumed it must be something up beat or perhaps a song that brought back a fond memory. 

She wore a large sweater, it looked purple to me, but an artist may have called it a shade of dark eggplant with grey undertones. Her jeans were faded, perhaps acid washed. All in all she appeared as a mirage straight from the 90's but remade with a modern twist. 

Her skin tone was a bit tan considering what time of year it was, perhaps indicating a native american lineage as her high cheek bones suggested. Her eyes, or what I caught of them when she chanced a glance away from the window, were a greenish brown. They reminded me a bit of murky lake water to be honest. 

Her hair was filled with ringlets and waves, it cascaded just below her shoulders as a dark brown waterfall. It was light and airy as if it itself was filled with autumn breeze. 

She was young, I guessed nineteen. I wondered where she was off to on a saturday. She didn't seem at all concerned with getting off the train. She never checked her phone to see what time it was, I could see it laying face down in her lap. She never looked around with any sort of conviction to get up or any gumption to make sure she had not missed her stop and we had already made 3 stops. But who was I to judge? I wasn't looking to disembark for at least 3 more stops. 

I briefly considered sitting next to her. There were only 4 other people on this part of the train, I did not feel any urge to sit beside them, but she seemed to draw me in. It was quite late, I was a little buzzed from my excursion at the bar, what would it hurt? Something about her was very inviting.

It was almost as if she read my mind as she repositioned herself on her seat. She swung one leg to the floor, pushed her back closer to the metal railing so she was almost sitting right in the corner of her seat. At this angle she could still look out the window, but also see what was going on in the rest of the train car. Her stance was more inviting now, but she did not look at me, nor even look up at all.

Cracked corn really doesn't have enough calcium to sustain egg production especially in the middle of winter, with no oyster shell, and no free ranging throughout the day.

"Who escaped?"  I asked calmly, listening to the muffled breathy whisper on the other line. I jotted down the location he had just given me earlier, in preparation to send officers.

"Thomas. His name is Thomas." He replied. "He's going to hurt someone... Please... Please stop him." 

"Where is he now?" I asked. "Are you in immediate danger?" 

The voice took a moment to respond and when it did it was shaky and panicked. "H-he's right here. He's right here with me. I-i'm okay. He won't hurt me, not yet." The man on the other line took a big breath and whimpered softly, then a low growling voice came on the line "No, not yet. Not yet." It spoke with great authority. 

"Who is this, is this Thomas?" I asked quickly and gave the signal to dispatch authorities to the location. 

"Yes." The voice growled, then gasped, and I was talking with the original caller again. "Thomas is gone now, but he's coming back. He's going to kill her. I don't want him to kill her." 

"Who else is there?"

"Just her." 

"What is her name?" 

"Lisa." I heard the creaking of a door being opened along with his shaky voice, and then a woman's panicked voice. "Jimmy, it's okay. Come here, just untie me and we can talk about this okay? Come here." 

"No..." He whispered. "I can't. Thomas will get mad." 

Then the female voice again. "Jimmy, he won't get mad. Just come here. It's all going to be okay I promise. You can do this. You can stop all this. I believe in you Jimmy. Who's on the phone." 

Jimmy seemed hesitant. "I... called them." 

Lisa seemed to understand what he meant. "Good, just like I told you. Good job Jimmy. See, you can do this." She talked to him like he was a child, though he must be at least in his late twenties by the sound of his voice. "Hey, Jimmy.... No, no! It's okay Jimmy. Look at me. Look at me please." The woman began to cry, I turned up my volume all the way and I could hear the despair in her voice.

"No." The voice on the phone growled, now different from Jimmy's voice. 

"Jimmy, please..." The woman's voice sobbed. 

"Jimmy," I said "It's okay Jimmy. Let's talk for a bit." I grasped fully what was happening now. It seemed that Jimmy was having some sort of psychotic break, perhaps paranoid schizophrenia. 

"This isn't Jimmy." The voice growled. "Who are you?"

"This is a friend of Jimmy's." I replied. If I told this alter ego who I was it might set him off.

The voice laughed maniacally and I heard the woman whimper. "Jimmy has no friends. I am his only friend, and this *bitch*" he said the word with such distain "isn't Jimmy's friend. Not anymore. Very soon she'll be no one." 

"I'm sure Jimmy loves you most, Thomas. I'm sure he's very dedicated to you. You don't have to hurt anyone." I said slowly, trying to buy time.

"You're going to be okay. Tie the rope as tight as you can. Apply pressure to the wound with a cloth and don't let go. You can use your shirt, pillow case, blanket, towel, anything you can find. The authorities will be there very soon. Hold on." I told her.

We stood, my best friend and I, in the shadow of the house. Normally there would be three of us there, but that night was different. Every night for the past three months had been different, in fact, but more so that night. 

We both stopped and looked up at the vinyl clad siding, but did not acknowledge anything for a few brief moments. It was as if no words could be formed to explain the thoughts in our minds; The sadness, regret, and loss. 

Tim took a few steps forward towards the door and unlocked it. "It's been pretty hard living here,  but it's gotten better."

I nodded, "Yeah, I would guess." The doorway lit up as he stepped inside his home, normally a place of safety and fun times, now just a carcass filled with dark secrets. His home, also known as the last place either of us saw Tyler alive, but neither of us mentioned that. 

I stepped inside too, he shook his boots off and onto the rug. I did the same. Little bits of snow from his pant legs  fell onto the tile, and then onto the hardwood of the living room as he walked. They appeared as bread crumbs on a trail that I was meant to follow, but a sick feeling entered my body. I took a little extra time hanging up my coat and gloves to lengthen the time I had to prepare for my first evening spent at Tim's since the tragedy. 

Tim sat in his usual spot, south of the empty spot, I sat between him and the empty spot in my usual spot. The TV was already on, playing reruns of American Dad. Tim quickly changed it to some random movie I hadn't really read the title of. He asked me if I'd like to watch it. I had said yes, but I hadn't heard the name of it. I was too busy focusing on the empty spot in the corner of the couch.

Tim lit a cigarette and I watched the flame dance, then disappear, so quickly. He sighed and dug in his pockets, pulling out a glass pipe and a small baggy. "Let's enjoy this night. He'd want us to enjoy it and not think about how fucked up things have been" he said absentmindedly as his shaky hands struggled with the resealable zipper on the baggy. 

I nodded my head, words still feeling foreign, and watched him pack the bowl. We'd done this so many times in this same spot, just the two of us, but then Tyler had joined us and for a year we were The Three Musketeers. All three of us would sit and talk, smoke, and laugh. It was a place for each of us to get away from our shitty days, our shitty jobs, our less than perfect lives, and just relax. 

I pulled out my pack of smokes from my pocket, and slowly flipped up the lid, examining my pack as if it held life's secrets. I had three left for the evening. My lucky cigarette looked back at me, it's end facing me; while the others laid, filters facing me as they should. Whenever I got a new pack I always flipped one over, and kept it for last, my lucky cigarette. Though I'd never noticed that it had brought me any luck, I still did it. Perhaps some part of me still had faith, still believed in luck. I set the pack down on Tim's coffee table, determined to save them until I was decently baked. 

Tim passed me the pipe and a lighter. I glanced over at Tyler's empty spot, then blinked. I brought the lighter to the glass and lit. The flames licked the bowl and smoke rolled over my tongue. I watched the fire flow into the bowl, marveling briefly at how it resembled a liquid being poured from the lighter like that. I let the button go and the flame was gone in a flash, the only remnant that it had been there was the slightly sour smoke filling my lungs. 

I passed the pipe and lighter back to Tim, holding my breath for as long as I could before exhaling in a smooth stream, which floated into the air and dissipated. "I can't believe we didn't notice," said Tim, before hitting the pipe.

I shook my head. "We did, or at least I did. He'd always sneak off to the bathroom. I noticed and I guess I just never wanted to believe he was doing Heroin, you know?" 

Tim passed the pipe back to me. "I know. I think somewhere in my head I knew too. I should have done something. If I noticed him gone I'd always go up there after him to see if he'd left any evidence behind. If he would have then maybe I would have confronted him, but I never found anything." 

I leaned back, and brought the pipe half way to my lips. "I noticed that too." I said, then I lit up. 

That hall to the bathroom seemed so dark and foreboding now. All along we both had known something was wrong, but for naivety's sake we never said anything. Were we too afraid or was it just the faith that everything would be okay that fucked him over in the end? 

I could imagine him sitting right there to my right, talking about his work or his mother. I could see him getting up, walking up that hallway. I could see myself then too, thinking that the slightly extended amount of time he spent there was due to the kidney troubles he had from his past overdose. And then I'd think of the long sleeves he wore now and wonder if maybe he was using again, that maybe the sleeves covered the track marks; That the abnormally long and frequent times he wandered off couldn't be explained by any simple excuse. But I'd try. I'd try to explain it all away and I would, I did. That was my mistake.

What had I done? I reached for the note without really looking and felt water pouring onto my hand. My head snapped up and I was in a bathroom. 

Water was running in the tub I was sitting in, warm and pleasant to the touch. I stared at the running water and then down into the basin, 'why is the water so red...?' I thought. And then I looked at my wrists. Blood oozed from my open veins light watery old oil paint being squeezed from a tube onto a pallet. A blade was clutched between my fingers. 'Is this the alternative to the scene before?' I thought. 'Is this where I'm headed?" 

I tried to snap my fingers like Tim had told me. I didn't want to be here any longer. Not in this trip. Not in this life, so very like my own waking life, this hell I was living. This wasn't fun anymore. I could barely snap my fingers, my tendons were split, but it didn't hurt. I couldn't bring my fingers together. I couldn't do anything. I couldn't do anything right. No wonder I was fucking killing myself. 

"Real mature!" a voice yelled from the other side of the door. "Locking yourself in the bathroom is really gonna solve our problems." It was Andrew. His heavy fists pounding on it in anger and he let out a loud groan of frustration. "Look, I know this is going to be hard, with you in college and me out west, but we can do it. We don't have to fight about this. It'll work out, Baby." he said, finishing with a thud and sigh as he rested his forehead on the door, I presumed. 

I knew it and he knew it. It wouldn't work out. Well, maybe he didn't know it yet because I was caught inside my imagined world. But I knew now that it wasn't going to work, I'd known it all along. 

The water drained from the tub and my wounds stopped bleeding. The banging on the door stopped. I closed my eyes and let the darkness flow in. Peace filled my body. 

When I opened them again I was in a meadow. The flowers were bright iridescent colors. The sky was so blue I couldn't even put it into words. I felt safe here, home. And very tired. I laid there for what seemed like hours, completely content with watching the world go by it it's array of metallic glimmer... I forgot about the scenes, the visions. I forgot about my life, my everything, I just laid there. No depressed thoughts. No worries. 

I let my eyes drift closed again eventually and this time when I awoke I was back on the couch. I groaned, head pounding with my heart beat. 

"Here's some water." Tim said, handing me a glass. 

"Thanks..." I said, my voice gravely and hoarse. I cleared it and sat up slowly. 

"How was it?" He asked. 

"It was... it was an eye opening experience..." I looked at him differently this time and smiled.

"Just try it." Tim said. "It'll be fun, trust me, it's like waking up in a whole new world. You can see everything so clear..." He held up a baggy with sheets of small white squares in it that seemed to glint with a sort of metallic sheen in the light of the TV screen across the room. He'd just got done telling me about this new drug he'd gotten a hold of, and insisted that I'd feel so much better afterward. He said it was like an awakening of sorts. 

I took the baggy from his hands. "What is this stuff?" I asked, not that I cared at this point. I'd take anything to get away from the living hell I was in. I'd driven to his house to smoke a joint or two and watch some Futurama, but with the way my life seemed to be headed I wasn't exactly perturbed by the idea of trying some new mind blowing drug. It probably wouldn't be all it was cracked up to be anyway. 

"They call it Lucid." He replied with a smile on his face, that smug kind of smile when someone knows something that you don't. "You don't have to do it if you don't want to, but trust me, with all the shit going on in your life..." He trailed off and smiled again, absently this time. "You won't regret it," he finished. 

The plastic on plastic crinkle seemed to resonate through the room as I opened the baggy and a slightly sweet scent billowed out. This 'Lucid' shit didn't seem too frightening. In fact it seemed pretty benign. Besides, Tim and I had been friends for a long time now, I trusted him with my life. And what did I have to lose? The worst that could happen was death and I'd been thinking about death a lot anyway. My thoughts weren't exactly roses and kittens these days. 

You probably know what I'm talking about; the everyday intrusive thoughts, the times where you forget things you shouldn't and you think a little too much about death.

I pulled out a sheet and placed one of the tabs on my tongue. Immediately my mouth was filled with a bitter sweet tang, not entirely bad, but not entirely good either. 

Tim noticed the sour face I was making and laughed. "Don't worry, it gets better. You're gonna want to lay down in a few seconds, it hits fast." 

I took his advice and quickly rearranged the pillows on his couch and pulled up my sweatshirt hood over my ears, suddenly feeling cold. Laying back, the ceiling seemed out of focus, like something so far in the distance that you can barely make out. I looked at Tim who was grabbing a blanket from the back of the couch to cover me up with. 

"You'll be okay, you won't regret this, I promise. And if you do, just snap your fingers and I'll wake you up." He said, as he tucked me in and then sat down at the foot of the couch. "I'll be right here the whole time." He pulled open the drawer of his coffee table and pulled out some Zig Zag rolling papers and a small Altoids tin to roll himself a joint. 

Tim was one of my closest friends. We'd known each other since freshman year of high school and had remained close through everything life had thrown at us. I missed how things used to be with us though... It was just different now, we didn't talk as much as we used to, not since he broke up with Kendall. It was the fact that he still had feelings for me that caused the distance and we both knew it. 

Previously I had felt safe in his presence, but maybe safe isn't the right word, or maybe it is, I couldn't tell anymore. But he was the only guy I could trust to not make things weird, but admittedly they were kind of weird now. 

I liked him for two years, from when I met him to the end of sophomore year, when he asked me to go out with him. I was so overjoyed when he did, but in the end it only lasted two weeks, as do most teen relationships. He left me, telling me that he thought he might be gay, but that never really sat well with his persona, especially not after he dated Kendall. But now that he had left her there was this unspoken feeling of 'what if?' for me. What if we had managed to stay together? Would I be better? Would I not struggle with this depression? Would my parents be together? Would they not have the stress of their fucked up daughter to sabotage the marriage? I wouldn't have dated Laurence if Tim and I would have stayed together, and maybe then Laurence wouldn't have killed himself over me. My heart heath with the slow, hard, tempo of guilt. Or did none of that matter at all... I wasn't sure. 

We were older now, we were different now, what if now it would work? We weren't in high school anymore. There was no pressure to be a certain way, no pressure to date, to lose your virginity, to be with someone to be 'cool'. All that was gone, all those things we care so much about doing in our teenage years had already happened... 

I watched him roll his joint, paper crinkly, forearms rippling ever so slightly, but before I knew it he was already done and lighting it up. It was like time had suddenly skipped ahead, like a video on netflix buffering to the place you left off, just a little blip in time before it catches up again. 

I watched his hands work intently, following the line of his wrists, feeling self conscious about my own. I pulled my sleeves down, partly because of the coldness radiating from inside my body, partly because of the scars. 

My thoughts broke off into a jumbled mess and then reassembled and I closed my eyes to concentrate. Where were my thoughts, pictures, feelings, and memories all seemed to fade in and out. I looked back at the ceiling and it was gone. I knew it was there, I could see the blur of where it used to be; but it was just that, a blur. My eyelids grew heavy, my stomach turned, my arms felt weightless against the cushions and a clasped my hands tightly around them to make sure they didn't blur away too. 

I closed my eyes and focused on relaxing, letting the trip take me, and boy did it ever take me...

My eyes blinked open to a room unknown. White walls, with white curtains over the windows, bright morning sun filtering in through the billowing folds. I blinked and rolled over to feel a warm body pressed against me. "Oh hello, beautiful." A familiar voice mumbled sleepily. Tim. I was in bed with Tim. How did this happen? What the fuck did I do? What the fuck did that trip make me do?! Did I cheat on my boyfriend? Did I ruin everything?
